turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll read the vitals before you go through. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Temperature is thirty-eight point three.
[SEG0002] person_1 (NURSE): Pulse is seventy-six. Weight is sixty-two kilograms. Ag, sorry, wrong line on the screen, it's seventy-two kilograms.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Last time in March you were sixty-eight. Your last pressure was one-forty.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. That's, uh, fine I guess. I don't really know what half of that means.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's here for his back, sister. Three weeks now. It shoots down the left leg when he sits, and his toes go numb.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The leg, ja, but not the toes. I don't think they're numb. I don't know, maybe my wife feels it more than I do. It stops around the knee.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this computer is crawling. Say that again for me, what's brought you in?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): My lower back has been sore for about three weeks and it shoots down the left leg to the knee. That's why I came.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long, sorry, say the time again? The screen blinked.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. I don't know, doctor. About three weeks.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three weeks, yes. Started just after he helped move my brother's couch, then he was stuck at the robot for ages. Probably not relevant.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. What sets it off?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Sitting. I work in accounts so I'm at the desk the whole day. If I get up and walk it's a bit better. Lying down is alright too.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any tablets?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, ibuprophen. Four hundred milligrams by mouth, three times a day. Well, I'm meant to. Sometimes I forget the midday one.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And his colleague told him to do those floor stretches. He's been doing them after work.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Some of them. The twist one pulls, so I left that. I don't know if the others help, doctor.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any weakness in the leg? Trouble passing urine? Numbness in the saddle area, between the legs?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No weakness. Urine's fine. No numbness there. I don't know what saddle means exactly but no, nothing like that.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest, breathing, any of that?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Chest is fine. Breathing's normal.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicine?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergies.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's not right. Amoxicillin, years ago, he came out in a rash. He said they mustn't give it again.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, that was a heat rash. I'm not allergic. I don't know, doctor, it was hot that week.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. Sister, the temperature, read it again? I clicked off the chart.
[SEG0027] person_1 (NURSE): Thirty-eight point three. Pressure one oh nine over seventy-seven. And the weight is seventy-two kilograms, not sixty-two.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right, a bit warm then. On the bed, please. I'm lifting the left leg.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Straight leg raise on the left brings the pain at about forty degrees. The right leg lifts clean, no pain. Muscles are tender over the lower back. No foot drop.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yoh. Ja, that left one grabs. Sorry.

[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): This is most likely sciatica, the nerve being irritated. I can't say that for certain today, not until we see how it goes. The temperature is why I want bloods, not because I've made a diagnosis.

[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): The nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, a full blood count and a CRP. You don't need to fast, just pitch up in the morning. If those are borderline we do the third test, the ESR.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday morning. Ok. I don't know if my boss will moan, but ja.

[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll book physio for this coming week as well. Stop that twisting stretch. Keep walking, don't sit for hours on end. Carry on with the ibuprophen, four hundred milligrams three times a day, and try not to skip.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His brother had a scan for his back. Shouldn't he have one?
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not today. We might do a scan if it does not settle. I'll see you in two weeks, let's see how the leg is doing then.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. What if it gets bad before that? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the pain gets much worse, or you can't pass urine, or the leg goes weak, come straight back. Don't wait out the two weeks for that.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. The parking is going to run out, we left the car on the street.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put the bloods in for Thursday morning and send the physio referral today. See you Thursday.

spec.situation: Person with low back pain shooting down one leg for three weeks, worse sitting; takes ibuprofen; a colleague's advice on exercises; doctor examines straight-leg raise and plans physio, no scan yet.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

History of onset: back pain started just after helping move a couch.
Review of systems negative for chest symptoms as well as breathing symptoms; patient said chest is fine and breathing is normal.
Doctor advised urgent return not only for much worse pain, inability to pass urine, or leg weakness, but specifically not to wait the two weeks if these occur.
